titre: Rousseau: Rejecting Representatives (1762), Then Setting Limits on Them (1772)
accroche: Rousseau rejects represented sovereignty, yet ten years later he proposes to set limits on the Polish deputies: a refusal of principle, not a rejection.
contenu_vulgarise:
“The English people believes itself to be free; it is greatly mistaken.” Rousseau's sentence serves as a manifesto against political representation. Ten years later, however, he proposes rules to set limits on deputies.

## The Principle of *The Social Contract*

In Book III, chapter 15 of *Du contrat social* (*The Social Contract*, 1762), Rousseau starts from the observation that the idea of deputies or representatives was born, among other causes, from the cooling of love of country, the activity of private interest, and the immensity of states. He adds a barb about what is called in a certain country the “third estate”: the particular interest of two orders is put in first and second place there, the public interest in third. Then the principle: “Sovereignty cannot be represented, for the same reason that it cannot be alienated”; it consists in the general will, and “the will cannot be represented.” The deputies of the people “are therefore not and cannot be its representatives; they are only its commissioners.” Any law that the people in person have not ratified “is null.” Then comes the jab at England: the people there are free only during the election of the members of Parliament; as soon as they are elected, “they are a slave, they are nothing.”

## What Is Remembered Less

In the same chapter, Rousseau admits that the people may be represented in the executive power, which is merely force applied to the law. The refusal bears on sovereignty, that is, on the act of making the law.

## The *Considérations sur le gouvernement de Pologne* (*Considerations on the Government of Poland*), April 1772

Rousseau, to whom Count Wielhorski had communicated a memorandum on the customs of the Poles, studies the reform of their government. The text, published in 1782 in the collection of his works, first observes that in a large state the legislative power “can act only through deputation”: “This has its bad and its good, but the bad outweighs it.” Representatives are hard to deceive but easily corrupted. He proposes two remedies: frequent Diets, which often change the representatives and make seducing them more costly, and above all binding the representatives to follow their instructions exactly and to give a strict account of their conduct. The nuncios' instructions must be drafted with care, read, discussed, and consented to in assembly, handed to the deputies in writing, and the nuncio who has followed them to the satisfaction of his constituents may be “declared admissible once again”: the others are excluded from any subsequent nunciature.

## The Shift

*The Social Contract* describes what a sovereign people would be; the *Considerations* say what must be done when a large state rules that out. Rousseau does not turn his back on his principle: he makes the deputy a commissioner bound by his instructions and accountable for his conduct rather than a master. One may ask whether a mandate drafted by the assembly of voters remains the expression of a general will, or already that of a group.

repere.texte: Rousseau writes in April 1772: one must “bind the representatives to follow their instructions exactly and to give a strict account” of their conduct at the Diet to their constituents.

carte.punch: Rousseau rejects represented sovereignty, then sets limits on representation.
carte.idee: In The Social Contract (1762), Rousseau holds that sovereignty cannot be represented: deputies are only commissioners. In 1772, for Poland, he nevertheless binds them with instructions and an accounting.

quiz.question: What do the Considerations on the Government of Poland (1772) show in relation to The Social Contract?
choix: Rousseau abandons the principle of the people's sovereignty to defend an enlightened monarchy
He admits deputies, but bound by instructions and required to give an account
Rousseau recommends choosing deputies by lot to remove the risks of corruption
Rousseau defends a regime in which the Senate alone votes the laws on behalf of the nobility
quiz.explication: Rousseau keeps his principle but admits representation out of necessity: written instructions, an accounting, frequent Diets. He does not abandon the sovereignty of the people, does not propose choosing deputies by lot (lot enters his scheme only in the election of the king), and does not entrust the law to the Senate alone.

quiz_supplementaire.question: According to Book III, chapter 15 of The Social Contract, why does Rousseau assert that sovereignty cannot be represented?
choix: Because it is the general will, which is not represented
Because representatives cost too much to compensate
Because only nobles can be elected as representatives
Because representation is forbidden by Roman law
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Rousseau holds that sovereignty consists in the general will, and that “the will cannot be represented”: deputies are therefore only commissioners, never full representatives.

quiz_supplementaire.question: According to the passage cited from The Social Contract on England, when are the English people free?
choix: All the time, thanks to their parliamentary regime
Only during the election of the members of Parliament
Only when the king convenes Parliament
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Rousseau writes that the English people are free only during the election of the members of Parliament: once the deputies are elected, they are a slave, they are nothing, according to the text cited in the entry.

quiz_supplementaire.question: In this same chapter of The Social Contract, what exception to his refusal of representation does Rousseau admit?
choix: Representation is admitted for voting the state budget
Representation is admitted for the executive power, which applies the law
Representation is admitted for appointing judges
Representation is admitted for electing the sovereign
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Rousseau admits that the people may be represented in the executive power, which is merely force applied to the law: the refusal bears only on sovereignty, the act of making the law.
